title: Words Against the Wind
text:
The poem opens with a small boat moving across a dark lake. Its speaker stands on the shore and watches the light fade slowly behind the hills. The poet uses short lines to show how quickly the evening arrives.

In the final lines, the speaker decides to light a lamp and wait for the boat to return. The poem never says whether the boat comes back. This open ending invites the reader to decide what hope means in the story.

questions.text: What does the speaker watch in the first paragraph?
options: The light fading behind the hills

questions.text: What does the speaker decide to do in the final lines?
options: Light a lamp and wait for the boat
Row out to the middle of the lake
Leave the shore and go home
Write a letter to the boat's owner

questions.text: What can be inferred about the speaker's feelings toward the boat?
options: The speaker hopes that the boat will return
The speaker is angry at the boatman
The speaker has no interest in the boat
The speaker plans to sell the boat

questions.text: Why does the ending of the poem leave the reader uncertain?
options: It invites the reader to interpret hope
The poet forgot the final line
The speaker is asleep and cannot answer

vocabulary.definition: the land along the edge of a lake or sea
to gradually become less bright or less strong
a device that gives off light, often for a room or table
encourages someone to do something or consider something

paragraph_translations: Wiersz otwiera mała łódź płynąca przez ciemne jezioro. Mówiący stoi na brzegu i patrzy, jak światło powoli gaśnie za wzgórzami. Poeta używa krótkich wersów, aby pokazać, jak szybko nadchodzi wieczór.

W ostatnich wersach mówiący postanawia zapalić lampę i czekać na powrót łodzi. Wiersz nigdy nie mówi, czy łódź wróci. To otwarte zakończenie zaprasza czytelnika, aby sam zdecydował, czym jest nadzieja w tej historii.
